header: Date: 2026-11-30 | Time: 16:00 PST | Duration: 52m\nAttendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Tom Erickson (Umbra VP Eng), Maria Li (Umbra Security), Jordan Park (Umbra Network Lead), Leah Kim (Umbra Cloud)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — alex from Redwood, i'm the AE. quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Tom: Tom here.
[00:00:10] Maria: Maria on security.
[00:00:12] Jordan: Jordan, network.
[00:00:14] Leah: Leah, infra.
[00:00:16] Priya: Priya, solutions eng at Redwood. Diego also on.
[00:00:30] Alex: Great. purpose of today's call is to map Umbra's private connectivity needs for a potential Private deployment — really the VPC onramp: peering, private endpoints, egress, regions. we'll surface blockers and then agree next steps.
[00:00:50] Tom: High level context: we have a SaaS ML product, mostly in GCP us-west1 and europe-west1. data residency for EU customers is a must. our compliance team wants traffic to stay inside region where possible. latency target for inference is sub-80ms p95 for our 8k-context flows.
[00:01:12] Priya: ok, thanks. couple quick qualifiers: will you run models in-hosted Redwood or Dedicated GPUs inside your VPC or private? and what's your expected QPS / token rate?
[00:01:30] Jordan: Thinking private deployment, customer-managed VPC with a private control plane. QPS is modest today, maybe 20 rps peak, but we need headroom for spikes to ~120 rps during batch windows.
[00:01:45] Maria: and audit logs + KMS integration are mandatory. we use a cloud KMS right now, want to understand HSM options if needed.
[00:01:55] Priya: got it. so options we usually evaluate: VPC peering (simple), PrivateLink / Private Endpoint (more firewall-friendly), or transit gateway style attachments for multi-VPC. each has tradeoffs on routing, egress IPs and cross-region latency.
[00:02:15] Leah: a question on egress — if traffic leaves our VPC for Redwood managed infra, will that show as external egress for compliance? we need to track data flows for audits.
[00:02:28] Diego: good question — for Redwood Private we can do a private dataplane so traffic doesn't traverse the public internet; but depending on deployment mode you may still need NAT for egress, or use an egress VPC with NAT gateways. we'll send details.
[00:02:45] Alex: also important: where model inference runs — if it's in-region in your VPC then regional residency is preserved. for hosted variants we have regional hosting but it's still Redwood-managed.
[00:02:58] Tom: Can you clarify differences between Dedicated and Private here? we keep hearing both.
[00:03:05] Priya: sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity hosted in Redwood infra: we give you tenant isolation and committed throughput; network-wise you often use peering or a private link into Redwood's dedicated cluster. Private (VPC/on-prem) means Redwood control plane may be in our cloud but we deploy runtime into your VPC, or we ship an on-prem package. Private gives you full VPC routing control and data stays in your network.
[00:03:30] Alex: slight transcription note — sometimes our product names get munged in calls, but the important thing is the network pattern.
[00:03:40] Jordan: technical: we prefer AWS Transit Gateway for central egress and have spokes for each account. would Redwood support a transit gateway attachment?
[00:03:50] Priya: yes — we have patterns for TGW attachments. typical approaches: 1) TGW attach straight to Redwood Private ENIs 2) use VPC peering per account 3) PrivateLink endpoints per region. for TGW you get central control but need route table coordination; peering is simpler but can be a pain at scale.
[00:04:12] Maria: security: do you support mutual TLS between our apps and the Redwood runtime? and can we bring our own certs / KMS keys?
[00:04:22] Diego: yes to mTLS in Private setups, and KMS integration is supported — we can plug into your cloud KMS. HSM-backed keys we need to discuss per-contract but feasible.
[00:04:35] Jordan: what's the egress IP behavior for model calls? we need stable egress IPs to whitelist in partner firewalls.
[00:04:45] Priya: we can provide static egress IPs for Dedicated/Private using NAT gateways in your VPC or by routing through controlled egress nodes. for Hosted API static IPs are harder but we do have allowlist options.
[00:05:00] Tom: region constraint: do you have runbooks for data residency? we can't have EU customer data processed in us-west.
[00:05:10] Alex: absolutely — Private deployment can ensure models are pinned to europe-west1 for EU work. we'll provide a region mapping doc.
[00:05:20] Maria: audit logs — are request logs stored in our tenant, or forwarded to our SIEM?
[00:05:28] Diego: we can forward logs to your log collector (S3/Cloud Storage or syslog) and also keep a copy in our control plane if you want. retention is configurable per contract.
[00:05:40] Leah: on throughput: if we need to scale from 20->120 rps, what's the autoscaling behavior? do you do warm pools?
[00:05:50] Priya: yes — autoscaling for Dedicated uses pre-warmed GPUs and model-variant based scaling. for Private in your VPC we support autoscaling via a node pool controller but that depends on your quota and automation. we can pre-warm a reserved burst capacity to meet spikes.
[00:06:08] Jordan: are there kernel/quantization constraints? we use some quantized 8-bit models to save footprint, want to know if the runtime supports it natively.
[00:06:18] Diego: our runtime supports quantized execution paths and we select kernels based on model arch and sequence lengths, but we should run a quick perf bench.
[00:06:26] Tom: bench — would you be open to running a 2-hour perf test in our environment? we can provide sample prompts and traffic patterns.
[00:06:34] Priya: yep that's standard — we'll need an infra window and a test VM or small k8s cluster to attach. expected steps: 1) exchange network allowlist 2) deploy agent 3) run tests 4) share metrics.
[00:06:48] Maria: on compliance: SOC2 + ISO are required; if we go to Private we need articulation of data flows for the audit. can you provide a package?
[00:06:58] Alex: yes we'll share our compliance pack. note some customers request a redacted SOC report and an ISA.
[00:07:05] Tom: vendor question — have other telco/edge companies used Redwood in Private? curious about connectivity at scale.
[00:07:12] Priya: yes, we've onboarded edge-heavy customers and have patterns for peering and edge egress. will send case snippets (redacted).
[00:07:22] Jordan: NAT & port mapping specifics — if we do VPC peering we can't use overlapping CIDRs. we have a lot of accounts, so peering scale is a concern.
[00:07:32] Diego: that's the classic reason customers prefer PrivateLink or TGW. PrivateLink only needs endpoints and avoids CIDR overlap, but it's per-region.
[00:07:44] Leah: cross-region replication of model cache — does Redwood replicate the model weights or do you serve from central model store?
[00:07:53] Priya: for Private we can pull artifacts into local storage in your region to avoid cross-region traffic; for hosted we serve from our model store and replicate as needed.
[00:08:05] Tom: let's talk about timeline — we're aiming to pilot in Q1. what's a realistic ramp if we sign a pilot in mid-December?
[00:08:15] Alex: pilot timeline: 2-4 weeks for network setup and basic connectivity, 2 weeks for perf bench and prom/reject criteria, then a 4-6 week pilot to validate reliability and cost. so mid-December sign could lead to a Jan pilot start.
[00:08:30] Maria: cost/security tradeoff — we need to know cost delta for keeping everything in-region private vs hosted.
[00:08:37] Priya: we'll produce an estimated cost model for Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted including egress and quantization savings. Diego will own throughput numbers.
[00:08:45] Jordan: any limitations on Transit Gateway bandwidth or attachments you anticipate?
[00:08:52] Diego: not from the runtime side — it's more your cloud quota and serializing attachments. we recommend testing with a smaller spike first.
[00:09:02] Tom: are there recommended MTU or jumbo frame settings for performance? our infra uses jumbo frames across accounts.
[00:09:10] Priya: we have guidance; jumbo frames are usually fine but we need to validate with the network team during bench.
[00:09:18] Alex: quick call-out — we'll put together a peering checklist, allowed ports (typically 443, some ephemeral for control plane), expected CIDR mapping and sample route tables.
[00:09:32] Maria: and please include SSO/SAML provisioning steps for RBAC tie-in.
[00:09:38] Diego: will do, include SCIM flow for user sync.
[00:09:44] Alex: i want to surface a couple of friction items we often see: overlapping CIDRs, constrained egress IPs, and firewall deep-packet inspection that could break TLS. expect us to propose a private endpoint if any of those are present.
[00:09:58] Tom: noted.
[00:10:02] [00:10:02] (short silence / background rustle)
[00:10:20] Jordan: curious about rollback and failover — if a region goes down do you have automatic fallback to another region and does that violate residency?
[00:10:30] Priya: good question — by default fallback can go to a cross-region model variant but for strict residency we can disable cross-region fallback and rely on local redundancy. it's a tradeoff: availability vs residency policy.
[00:10:47] Maria: so we may want a canary policy: if EU is down, degrade gracefully but don't send production EU requests to US.
[00:10:56] Diego: we support canary rollouts and region pinning.
[00:11:02] Tom: network ops items — we'll need an RFC to our cloud infra team. Jordan and Leah will draft.
[00:11:08] Leah: timeline wise, would Redwood need service account keys or cross-account role?
[00:11:14] Priya: usually we ask for an IAM role with limited privileges for artifact pulls and logging sink writes; for Private deployments we can run as your service account in your VPC.
[00:11:26] Alex: all right i'm going to jump ahead to recap; but before that any blockers we haven't covered?
[00:11:34] Maria: compliance nuance: can we get a whitepaper on log retention and encryption at rest for the control plane?
[00:11:40] Diego: yes, add to next steps.
[00:11:45] Tom: nothing else from me.
[00:11:48] Alex: recap / next steps: 1) Alex will send network diagram + peering checklist and compliance pack by 2026-12-03, 2) Priya & Diego will prepare perf test plan and throughput estimate by 2026-12-05, 3) Jordan to share VPC CIDRs and TGW IDs by 2026-12-02, 4) schedule infra deep-dive for 2026-12-07.
[00:12:20] Tom: sounds good.
[00:12:24] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links to docs.
[00:12:30] (meeting wraps)
[00:13:00] [Transcript continues with some Q&A threads and clarifications — lower-volume chatter and background typing. Imperfect ASR, occasional speaker mislabels like "Speaker 2" for Diego are present in raw export. Example snippets below:]
[00:13:16] Speaker 2: umm so the port list again?
[00:13:20] Alex: 443 for control plane, 8443 for metrics in some deploys, and ephemeral 49152-65535 for certain k8s agent flows — we'll provide exact ACL.
[00:13:38] Speaker 1: can you repeat the bench steps?
[00:13:41] Priya: exchange allowlist, deploy the agent, run synthetic traffic and replay logs, share results.
[00:13:55] Speaker 3: is there a preferred latency threshold for the bench?
[00:13:59] Diego: we'll aim to replicate your sub-80ms p95 target and capture tail latencies.
[00:14:10] (background murmur)
[00:14:40] Maria: one more compliance nit — do you support data subject access request workflows if customers request deletion?
[00:14:48] Alex: yes, in Private we can honor DSARs by removing tenant data; in hosted we have documented processes.
[00:14:56] Tom: ok that's the list. appreciate the clarity.
[00:15:05] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription shows some ASR errors (product names sometimes mangled, speaker numbers appear in parts). Attachments mentioned: redwood_private_vpc_onramp.pdf, peering_checklist.xlsx, SOC2 summary link.
